target_customer: restaurants (owners/operators) wanting table-side ordering and payment
problem: Diners wait for servers to order, get the check and pay; restaurants lose impulse orders and table turns when staff are busy.
business_model: SaaS/hardware subscription to restaurants after a 30-day free trial; post-trial pricing undecided as of launch coverage
product_category: restaurant tech: table-side tablet / mobile ordering and payment

founders.name: Sam Brin
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2013-07-30) gave his age as 26 and called him the younger brother of Google co-founder Sergey Brin, who advised but did not invest.

founders.name: Jon Li
founders.background_notes: Described as Sam Brin's college friend.

competitors.name: E La Carte
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch said it had worked on the problem for a while with varying success

technical_complexity.rationale: A menu/order/payment app on tablets and phones is standard mobile and POS-integration work; no research-grade problem is evident from the launch coverage.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch headlined the space as crowded, with E La Carte, iMenu, MenuPad and 'countless others' offering similar products, and no unique asset or lock-in was described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Presto (restaurant tablets) later became a notable player; Butter shows as Inactive on YC with no acquisition or pivot reported.

market_need_then: Restaurants had a pain point in server availability, table turn and impulse ordering; Butter was in beta at one restaurant (Bumble, Los Altos) with referrals by word of mouth, but no revenue or customer counts were reported.
outcome_analysis: Butter Systems was a two-person YC company that launched a table-side tablet menu in a market TechCrunch called crowded, with beta testing at a single restaurant and no disclosed funding. YC lists it as Inactive, but no shutdown announcement, post-mortem, acquisition or pivot was found, so the cause is unknown; a low-quality aggregator attributes it to weak differentiation, which fits the crowded field but is unverified.
notes: Batch conflict: TechCrunch and Crunchbase say Winter 2013; the YC directory says Summer 2013. Founded year not stated by any source seen, so left null. Age 26 is as of the 2013-07-30 article, treated as age at founding (founding year 2013 is approximate). Crunchbase page was not fetched; funding unknown, not zero. Aggregator claim on failure reason is not a reliable source. Completeness pass: one seed round with Fenox Venture Capital and undisclosed amount rests on a single outlet (FinSMEs); the 2013-10-15 date came from a database listing seen only in a search summary. A report that Crunchbase showed $100k seed is not recorded because the source was not opened. Total raised unknown.
